title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
summary: Given a matrix and a target, count the number of non-empty submatrices whose sum equals the target.
statement: Given a matrix and a target, count the number of non-empty submatrices whose sum equals the target. A submatrix is defined by coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2) where x1 <= x <= x2 and y1 <= y <= y2. Submatrices are considered different if any coordinate differs.
constraints: Matrix values and target may be negative.
Count all nonempty rectangular submatrices summing to target.
hints: Fix top and bottom rows to collapse the rectangle problem into one-dimensional column sums.
For each collapsed array, count target-sum subarrays with prefix frequencies.
Repeat for every row pair, seeding prefix zero once.
Every rectangle has one unique top-bottom pair and one contiguous column interval counted exactly once.
editorial: Every rectangle has one unique top-bottom pair and one contiguous column interval counted exactly once.

tests.explanation: The four corner singleton zeros are the only zero-sum rectangles.
